worked_exemplar.historical_question: As of 2024-03-01, will the monthly 3-month yield change for United States 3-month Treasury yield in 2024-03 be at least -0.015 percentage points?
worked_exemplar.target_semantics: The question asks whether the absolute change in the US 3-month Treasury yield during March 2024 will be greater than or equal to -0.015 percentage points.
expert_reasoning: The target is the monthly change in the 3-month US Treasury yield for March 2024. This requires observing the yield at the end of February 2024 and the end of March 2024.
The calculation involves subtracting the February yield from the March yield to determine the absolute change. This change must then be compared against the threshold of -0.015 percentage points.

The historical DAG indicates that the direct observations of the yield at the start and end of the period are key drivers, as is the calculation of their difference and comparison to the pre-registered threshold.
worked_exemplar.counterevidence: No forecast-time evidence was provided to support or contradict any aspect of the yield change calculation or the threshold comparison.
worked_exemplar.prospective_target_estimate: The provided DAG structure and lack of evidence prevent a prospective estimate. The historical support for the relevant checkpoints is medium to strong, but without current data, the direction of change and its magnitude relative to the threshold remain unknown.
worked_exemplar.option_mapping: The 'yes' option corresponds to a monthly yield change of -0.015 percentage points or greater (i.e., less negative or positive). The 'no' option corresponds to a monthly yield change less than -0.015 percentage points (i.e., more negative).
worked_exemplar.uncertainty: Significant uncertainty exists due to the complete absence of forecast-time evidence. The DAG highlights that the underlying yield observations and the resulting change calculation are critical, but without current data, their values and direction are unknown.
worked_exemplar.dag_derived_lesson: When forecasting a change metric, direct observation of the metric's constituent values at the relevant time points is crucial. The calculation mechanism linking these values to the change, and the subsequent comparison to a defined threshold, must also be supported by current evidence. Reliance on historical structure alone is insufficient without current data to validate the causal paths.
